verdict.reasoning: Patient states, "I keep having a headache," indicating headache as the presenting complaint.
Patient says, "It started yesterday... Yesterday, about mid morning."
Patient describes location: "It's on the left side at the back," consistent with left occipital region.
Patient describes the pain as "quite intense and kind of quite throbbing."
Patient states, "It kind of built up gradually over a short period of time."
When asked 0–10, patient responds, "Say about 8."
To positional triggers, patient answers "No" to "any difference if you lie down, stand up, bend over, cough or sneeze" indicating the headache is not positional.
When asked, "Has it been worse at any particular time of the day?" patient responds, "No, it hasn't made any difference," indicating no diurnal pattern.
Doctor asks, "did you manage to sleep through the night?" Patient replies, "Yes, I did."
Patient: "I took some Nurofen yesterday." Doctor: "did that make any difference?" Patient: "Not really."
Doctor asks, "in the past, have you had any headaches before?" Patient: "Not really," indicating no or very rare prior headaches.
Doctor asks, "have you had your blood pressure checked?" Patient responds, "No, not recently."
Doctor asks, "have you got any other medical problems?" Patient: "No, I haven't."
Doctor: "Anything you take medication for?" Patient: "No, I don't," indicating no regular medications.
Patient states, "I took some Nurofen yesterday... Ibuprofen."
Doctor asks, "Any over the counter medications or allergies?" but the patient only replies about Nurofen and does not explicitly deny allergies; no drug-allergy status is documented.
Patient: "My mother's had hypertension..."
Patient continues, "and she does get migraines."
To "Who do you live with at home?" patient answers, "My partner."
Patient states, "I'm a designer."
Doctor: "And do you smoke at all normally?" Patient: "No, I don't."
Doctor: "Do you drink any alcohol regularly?" Patient: "No."
Doctor: "And any other drugs?" Patient: "No." This supports no illicit drug use.

Patient says, "No, but I don't feel that I'm finding it really hard to do any of my work or normal things." The initial "No" answers "Have you had to miss any work at all?", meaning she has not missed work, so the fact is actually SUPPORTED, not contradicted.
Transcript supports: 1-day duration ("started yesterday"), left posterior location ("left side at the back"), throbbing quality, severe intensity ("about 8").
Doctor asks about "tingling, numbness, weakness anywhere?" Patient: "No, nothing," indicating no focal neurological symptoms.
Patient denies fever, shivery, sweaty, vomiting, and rash when directly asked, indicating no systemic red flag symptoms reported.
On prior headaches, patient says, "Not really," which the assessment summarizes as no prior history of headaches.
Doctor: "trying slightly stronger pain relief. So similar to ibuprofen, but taking it instead of ibuprofen, not at the same time, and taking that regularly with food."
Doctor specifies to take new pain relief "instead of ibuprofen, not at the same time," instructing not to combine with ibuprofen.
Doctor: "You can take paracetamol along with that."
Doctor advises, "Try and take rest..."
Doctor continues, "have lots of good hydration."

Doctor advises to seek help if "the pain's getting worse or you get new symptoms, feel fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, or you keep getting episodes of the same type of thing, then we need to speak to you..."
Doctor: "If it's getting worse or not settling in the next day or two, then certainly give us a call back when you try the medication that I prescribed."
Same as plan-007: doctor instructs call back "in the next day or two" if not settling.
Doctor asks about "Any nausea, vomiting" and later "Are you feeling sick or vomiting or anything?" Patient answers "No, nothing" and "No, nothing like that."
To "Any ... tingling, numbness, weakness anywhere?" patient says, "No, nothing."
Doctor: "Any blurred vision or any pain over your eyes?" Patient: "No."
Doctor: "Any funny lights or anything like that in your vision area?" Patient: "No."
Doctor: "Any problems when you look into the light?" Patient: "No."
Doctor: "Any high fever? Are you feeling shivery, sweaty?" Patient: "No, no fever." This implies no fever, chills, or sweats.
Doctor: "Any rashes at all?" Patient: "No."
Doctor: "And if you've been eating and drinking, okay?" Patient: "Yes. Yes."
